digest.component_or_area: inbound parent-field reconciliation and binding-store baseline tracking
propositions: A local parent_id must not be cleared based solely on managed_refs state, because managed_refs only records local writes, never whether the peer ever carried that parent, leading to silent data loss when a parent was set locally but never pushed to the peer.

A parent clear in the inbound direction requires positive evidence that the peer once had the parent; this evidence must be persisted as per-binding baseline state and advanced only when the parent key is observed in a snapshot, never on fail-open reads that degrade to empty.

The inbound parent-clear path must distinguish three observable states of the snapshot parent field—unobserved (key absent), observed-absent (key present, falsy), and unresolvable (key present, does not resolve to local id)—and emit a clear only for the observed-absent state when peer evidence exists.

A truncated or failed parent-map read must never overwrite a good peer-parent observation, or the next pass will read a deletion and re-attempt an already-destructive clear on a binding that has learned nothing new.

Same-pass outbound suppression alone cannot gate the clear, because the outbound parent-write is structurally unreachable on non-epic parents and most tickets, leaving the inbound clear unsuppressed in the common case.
